root_cause.text: A race condition in tls_sw_cancel_work_tx() where cancel_delayed_work_sync() does not prevent a new delayed work item from being scheduled (via tls_sw_write_space()) after the cancel completes, leading to the TX work handler dereferencing a freed TLS context.
root_cause.evidence: The commit description details the race on CPU0: setting BIT_TX_SCHEDULED then calling cancel_delayed_work_sync, while CPU1 concurrently tests-and-sets the same bit and schedules delayed work after the cancel returns, bypassing the intended barrier. The fix replaces cancel_delayed_work_sync with disable_delayed_work_sync to atomically disable future scheduling.

candidates.rationale: Setting BIT_TX_CLOSING is intended to indicate that TX is closing, but the race condition allows a new delayed work to be scheduled after cancellation, making this flag insufficient to prevent scheduling.

Setting BIT_TX_SCHEDULED may be used to track scheduling, but the race condition allows a new work item to be scheduled after cancel_delayed_work_sync, indicating that this flag does not prevent the race.

This is the primary vulnerable statement: cancel_delayed_work_sync() does not guarantee that a new delayed work item (triggered by tls_sw_write_space()) cannot be scheduled after it returns, leading to a race condition and use-after-free.
